assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of the cell is a genuinely new concept of molecular organisation: membraneless compartments (P granules, nucleoli, stress granules) arise from thermodynamic phase behaviour of multivalent, partly disordered biomolecules. It recasts cell biology in the language of phase diagrams, wetting, surface tension and scaling that physical chemistry supplies, and its reach into neurodegeneration and amyloid-like ageing is large.
assessment.attribution: The 2009 P-granule liquid-droplet demonstration (Brangwynne and Hyman) and the multivalent-interaction phase-transition work (Rosen, Li et al. 2012) are the decisive conceptual and experimental steps. Pappu and Mittag supply essential sequence-grammar and theory, but a three-person prize of Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen is the most natural configuration, though it leaves out important contributors.
assessment.maturity: Strongly reproduced across many systems and widely adopted; the concept is mature. Still, how far in-cell condensates are true equilibrium phase separation and which are functionally relevant is actively debated, so timing is good but the interpretation is not fully settled.
uncertainties: Debate over whether many reported cellular condensates are genuine phase separation versus artefacts of overexpression or in vitro conditions.
Credit allocation among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag is not clean; I am relying on my own recollection of the key papers.
The prize may be judged as cell biology or physiology rather than chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a lipid self-assembly and colloid-chemistry solution to the long-standing problem of delivering nucleic acids: pH-dependent charge, controlled lipid phase and particle formation make endosomal escape possible. Their impact is enormous as the delivery vehicle behind siRNA therapy (patisiran) and the mRNA COVID-19 vaccines. This sits close to my own field of lipid assembly and membrane physics.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues established the rapid-mixing formulation and ionizable lipid concept; MacLachlan advanced SNALP and optimized ionizable lipids, and Anderson and Langer contributed lipidoid and polymer delivery materials. Hope and Madden were also key early contributors, so selecting three is hard, and the exact boundaries depend on patent and publication history I cannot verify.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation at global scale is unusually strong and independent; recognition is timely, though the mRNA vaccine prize in Medicine (2023) already covers the nucleoside-modification half of the story.
uncertainties: Which three of Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer are most decisive is disputed.
Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize may reduce committee appetite.
Commercial and patent disputes may colour the credit narrative.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The energy-landscape and funnel picture resolved Levinthal's paradox and gave protein folding a statistical-mechanical, thermodynamic foundation, linking sequence, frustration, kinetics and structure. It is a deep physical-chemical concept that shaped folding theory, simulation and experiment, and underlies later thinking about disordered proteins and aggregation.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic (with Bryngelson, Leopold) developed the principle of minimal frustration and funnel landscapes; Dill contributed lattice models and the hydrophobic-collapse view; Fersht provided key experimental phi-value mapping but his work is more experimental. Wolynes, Onuchic and Dill is a defensible trio but Bryngelson and Fersht are real alternatives.
assessment.maturity: The concept is long established and broadly accepted. It is perhaps overtaken in practical impact by AI structure prediction, but that does not weaken its conceptual standing.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as chemistry or biophysics/theory.
Credit between Wolynes, Onuchic, Bryngelson and Dill is a real unresolved allocation.
Recent AI structure-prediction prizes may reduce interest in folding theory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation reframes drug action as induced proximity and exploits the ubiquitin-proteasome system to remove proteins that were considered undruggable; the discovery that thalidomide-class molecular glues work via cereblon was a mechanistic breakthrough. It is a new chemical concept with broad therapeutic reach and many clinical-stage compounds.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies (PROTAC concept and first demonstrations, with Sakamoto) and Handa (cereblon as thalidomide target, with Ito) are central; Ciulli and Gray drove later VHL ligands and degrader chemistry. A trio of Crews, Deshaies and Handa is plausible but disregards the PROTAC versus molecular-glue split.
assessment.maturity: Many degraders are in clinical trials but approvals are still lacking, so clinical vindication is not yet complete; the concept itself is well reproduced and independently confirmed.
uncertainties: Possible premature recognition before first approved PROTAC drugs.
Compound candidate: PROTACs and molecular glues may deserve different recognition.
Sakamoto, Ito, Ciulli and Gray credit questions remain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-assembled monolayers of thiols on gold and soft lithography established the general idea that surfaces can be controlled at molecular level through spontaneous organisation, a classic surface and colloid chemistry concept. It enabled microfluidics, biointerfaces, molecular electronics and printing, and is a clear example of materials chemistry from physical-chemical principles.
assessment.attribution: Nuzzo and Allara reported the first thiol/disulfide monolayers on gold (1983); Whitesides greatly developed SAMs and soft lithography; Sagiv's earlier silane monolayers and Xia's soft-lithography work complicate credit. Whitesides, Nuzzo and Allara is a reasonable trio.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with decades of independent confirmation; recognition is arguably late, which is acceptable but means the field has partly been absorbed into routine tools.
uncertainties: Credit priority between Sagiv, Nuzzo/Allara and Whitesides.
Age and availability of laureates; this may seem a retrospective prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion lets cells incorporate designed non-canonical amino acids at specified sites using orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs, turning protein chemistry into programmable chemistry in living organisms. It is an original, widely used tool with major effects on chemical biology, protein engineering and therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the orthogonal pair approach in E. coli and yeast; Chin extended to multicellular organisms and quadruplet codons and genomic recoding; Wang was an early collaborator in Schultz's lab. Mehl and Yokoyama also contributed; the trio is workable but not unique.
assessment.maturity: Highly reproduced and now a standard method, so mature; timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Credit among Schultz, Chin, Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama.
Contribution of the earlier Hecht and Chamberlin suppressor tRNA work is outside the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one DNA base to another without double-strand breaks, an elegant fusion of nucleoside deaminase chemistry with programmable targeting. Impact is clear in research and early clinical translation.
assessment.attribution: The cytosine and adenine base editors came from Liu's lab, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead authors; Nishida and Kondo contributed an independent deaminase-fusion editing approach. Liu, Komor and Gaudelli would be natural but the junior authorship is unusual for a prize.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced widely and first clinical results exist, but the field is only a decade old and the 2020 CRISPR prize makes a close follow-up on genome editing questionable.
uncertainties: Concern that genome-editing recognition was already given in 2020.
Unclear whether committee will credit trainees alongside Liu.
Overlap with B047 in Liu's contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Two-dimensional infrared spectroscopy gives time-resolved access to vibrational coupling, structure and hydrogen-bond dynamics in liquids, proteins and amyloid, with the clarity of a new physical-chemical method. It is ultrafast spectroscopy continuing from Zewail's femtochemistry prize.
assessment.attribution: Mukamel supplied the theoretical framework of multidimensional spectroscopy; Hamm, Zanni, Tokmakoff and Fleming developed and applied the experimental methods. The credit is spread over several contributors and any trio leaves out strong names.
assessment.maturity: Mature and well confirmed with several independent groups; applications to amyloid and water dynamics are relevant to soft matter. Impact is narrower than for other candidates.
uncertainties: Broad credit allocation across at least five people.
Impact beyond specialist spectroscopy is less clear.
Possible conflict with 2D electronic spectroscopy credit (Fleming).
